record.title: fix: a payload the scan limit cut short left no trace of having been cut short

notes: cmd/runtime-proxy/dlp.go:77 — the new truncated-clean path calls s.record(), which reaches reporter.send() synchronously inside the MCP handler with a 10s client timeout. Previously that blocking POST only happened on the rare findings path; it now fires for every payload over MaxBytes, which the commit message itself calls the ordinary case for tool results. The doc at cmd/runtime-proxy/dlp.go:139 ('best effort and never blocks the call it describes') was already inaccurate but now matters at a frequency that can add seconds to tool calls when the control plane is slow or down. Not a defect introduced here, but the change moves it onto a hot path.

internal/guard/guard.go:153 and internal/execution/contentscan.go:127 — the two production changes that actually widen the recording gate are only proven by internal/execution/scanlimit_live_test.go, which t.Skip()s without AGENTHUB_TEST_DSN (contentpolicy_live_test.go:164). The new internal/execution/contentscan_test.go:425 test only asserts the returned ContentOutcome.Outcome(), never that recordContentScan writes an entry, so in default CI both lines could be deleted with every test still green. This matches the repo's existing live-test convention, so it is a coverage gap rather than a vacuous test — each new test does fail on the unmodified code (Outcome() returned "audited" before).

cmd/runtime-proxy/scanlimit_test.go:145 calls inspect() with direction "응답" directly, bypassing the cmd/runtime-proxy/mcp.go:395 gate. Tool responses are only scanned when settings.ScanResponses is on, and AdminDLP.tsx states that is off by default — so the test's framing ('a 2 MB answer whose first 64 kB happened to be clean') only holds on deployments that turned 응답도 검사 on. The request direction (tool arguments) is the one that is always scanned.

Audit volume: a deployment that lowers MaxBytes now writes one dlp.model/dlp.flow/dlp.export/dlp.review/dlp.tool row per oversized payload, and each dlp.tool report also costs a UserByID + insert on the control plane (internal/api/dlp.go:180). The commit argues for this trade explicitly and the default MaxBytes is 256 KB, so it should stay rare in practice, but it is the operational risk of this change.

Scope check on the BASE_VERSION 0.24.0 -> 0.25.0 bump: justified — runtime-images.json lists cmd/runtime-proxy and internal/dlp among the base image's sourcePaths — and complete: BASE_VERSION, internal/buildinfo/buildinfo.go, compose.yaml, deploy/kubernetes/ollama-bridge.yaml and README.md all move together, and no stale agenthub-base:v0.24.0 reference remains. No migrations, no auth/permission/secret/deletion logic touched; the change is additive and revertible.

The new 'unscanned' outcome has no .status-unscanned CSS rule, but neither do 'audited' or 'redacted' — the badge falls back to default styling, consistent with the existing DLP outcomes. dlp.Result.Truncated is verified to propagate through scrubDecision's per-field merge (internal/execution/provenance.go:337), so the decision-record boundary really does see it. Result.Outcome()'s other callers (cmd/runtime-proxy/dlp.go:99 scanDecision, internal/execution/contentscan.go:67) can only be reached with non-empty findings, so none of them can newly return 'unscanned' by accident.
Verified locally: go build ./..., go vet on the touched packages, and go test ./... all pass; web tsc --noEmit is clean. web/dist is not tracked, so the three .tsx edits need no committed rebuild.
